motivation: The pooled exact-point recovery result showed higher one-year Thalassia re-recording when another seagrass remained after focal loss. This audit asks whether that association persists within the same stable transect, reducing confounding by persistent node-level habitat quality.

primary_population.sequence_rule: same frozen three-year exact-point loss sequences used by microsite_recovery_pathway_v1
primary_population.informative_node: stable transect node containing >=1 loss-year vegetated sequence and >=1 loss-year bare sequence

primary_hypothesis.statement: Within informative stable transects, meter marks retaining another seagrass in the Thalassia-loss year have higher one-year Thalassia return than meter marks becoming seagrass-bare.
primary_hypothesis.node_effect: For each informative node, compute return fraction among vegetated loss-year sequences minus return fraction among bare loss-year sequences.
primary_hypothesis.estimator: unweighted mean of node-specific differences so high-sampling nodes do not dominate
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: 95% node-bootstrap interval for the mean within-node difference entirely above zero

secondary_descriptive: number of informative nodes with positive, zero, and negative differences
event-weighted pooled difference within the informative-node subset

interpretation.supported: The habitat-continuity return association persists within stable transects, consistent with a microsite-scale continuity signal beyond broad node quality.
interpretation.unsupported: The pooled habitat-continuity return association does not remain robust within the same transects; persistent node-level habitat quality is a plausible explanation.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc reference-saturation audit of an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Within-node persistence does not establish facilitation; microsite substrate, residual rhizomes, fine-scale environment, or observation persistence can generate the same association.
Return remains recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not demographic recolonization.
Do not alter the informative-node rule, equal-node estimator, bootstrap unit, period, or event definition after opening node-specific differences.
